recommendations.title: Eliminate render-blocking resources
recommendations.description: Resources are blocking the first paint of your page. Consider delivering critical JS/CSS inline and deferring all non-critical JS/styles. Learn how to eliminate render-blocking resources.

recommendations.title: Minify CSS
recommendations.description: Minifying CSS files can reduce network payload sizes. Learn how to minify CSS.

recommendations.title: Minify JavaScript
recommendations.description: Minifying JavaScript files can reduce payload sizes and script parse time. Learn how to minify JavaScript.

recommendations.title: Reduce unused CSS
recommendations.description: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused CSS.

recommendations.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
recommendations.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript.

recommendations.title: Serve images in next-gen formats
recommendations.description: Image formats like WebP and AVIF often provide better compression than PNG or JPEG, which means faster downloads and less data consumption. Learn more about modern image formats.

recommendations.title: Reduce JavaScript execution time
recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to reduce Javascript execution time.

recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to minimize main-thread work

aiSummaries.text:
Here is a summary of the automated crawl results for **contentbloom.com**:

* **Limited Test Scope:** The automated scan was only able to access three pages before stopping. This is an unusually low number for a full website and indicates the test was incomplete. 
* **Key Risk:** Because only a fraction of the site was scanned, the vast majority of your web pages remain untested, leaving potential bugs, broken elements, or performance issues undetected.
* **Likely Cause:** This typically occurs when the testing tool hits a roadblock, such as broken navigation links, login requirements, or security settings preventing deeper access.
* **Action Required:** The technical team needs to investigate why the crawler was blocked and re-run a full test once access is resolved.

aiSummaries.text:
Here is a summary of the recent broken link scan:

* **Key Finding:** Every page tested contains the exact same broken links, which indicates a site-wide issue in a shared template (such as the header or footer) rather than isolated page errors. 
* **Risks:** 
  * **Brand Credibility:** The company’s Facebook link is broken across the site, frustrating visitors trying to find your social media presence.
  * **Site Health:** An internal technical link (`xmlrpc.php`) is misconfigured and throwing an error on every page, which points to unnecessary background code being referenced.
* **Required Action:** Ask the web development team to update the global Facebook URL in the main site

aiSummaries.text:
- **Mobile Performance is Critically Low**: The average mobile score is 27, indicating significant performance issues that could negatively impact user experience and SEO. The worst-performing page on mobile takes over 14 seconds to load its largest content, which is far beyond acceptable standards.  
- **Desktop Performance is Acceptable but Can Improve**: The average desktop score is 75, which is decent but has room for improvement. Key issues include render-blocking resources and unused CSS.  
- **Common Issues Across Pages**: Eliminating render-blocking resources, minifying CSS, and reducing unused CSS are top priorities, affecting most pages. Properly sizing and deferring offscreen images are also important fixes.  
- **Action Needed**: Address mobile performance urgently, focusing on render-blocking resources and CSS optimization. Desktop improvements should follow to ensure a consistently fast experience across devices.
